_meta.basis: Consolidated (Syngene International Ltd and its three wholly owned subsidiaries: Syngene USA Inc (incl. the Bayview, Baltimore biologics site), Syngene Scientific Solutions Ltd and Syngene Manufacturing Solutions Ltd; AR FY26 Board's report). No minorities: Screener Net Profit = Profit for EPS in every year, so no patch is needed. Rs crore unless stated.

reuters.note: Reuters news feed (items dated Feb-2025 to Jul-2026 used)

profile.founded: 1993 in Bengaluru as a Biocon subsidiary; India's first contract research organisation; listed Aug-2015 (q1ppt pp.8, 29)
profile.parent: Biocon Ltd holds 211,185,608 shares = 52.41% (AR26 note 12; promoter group 52.59% at Jun-26, Screener). Biocon has sold down from 74.5% (Mar-17) to 52.4%: 5.4% for Rs1,220 cr (Sep-2022), 9.96% for ~Rs2,240 cr at ~Rs560 a share (Feb-2023, to help fund the Viatris biosimilars deal) and 80 lakh shares (~2%) for Rs686 cr (Dec-2024)

shares.note: Equity share capital Rs402.9 cr at Mar-26 (AR26 balance sheet); FY26 EPS Rs7.86 on Rs317 cr = ~40.3 cr weighted shares. The ESOP trust holds ~0.4% (q1ppt p.30).

profile.clients: ~400 active clients incl. 16 of the top 20 pharma companies; 400+ patents held by clients (q1ppt p.9)
profile.sites: ~3 mn sq ft across Bengaluru (HQ campus, BMS and other dedicated centres, biologics plants incl. Unit 3), Hyderabad (Genome Valley R&D), Mangaluru (commercial small-molecule API plant) and Baltimore, USA (Bayview biologics site) (q1ppt pp.7, 16; AR26)
profile.approvals: US FDA, EMA, UK VMD, Health Canada, PMDA approved sites; 85 client and regulator audits in FY26; 6 successful USFDA audits in five years (q1ppt pp.14, 19)
profile.models: Dedicated R&D centres (ring-fenced, typically 5+ years), FTE, fee-for-service, risk/reward and outcome-based contracts (q1ppt p.17)

fy26.exceptionalNote: FY26: Rs37.9 cr (net) net increase in gratuity liabilities under the new labour codes (Rs58 cr charge in Q3, Rs20 cr credit in Q4) and Rs25.3 cr (net) termination benefits; FY25: Rs21.3 cr (net) gain on final settlement of a 2016 fire insurance claim
fy26.src: ar26 MD&A p.193-194; consolidated P&L, notes 18-25, 33, 36; q4ppt p.27; q4call

top.note: Two customers above 10% of revenue in both years (AR26 note 33). Not named; our reading: BMS (largest collaborator, 700+ scientists in Bengaluru, contract extended to 2035) and Zoetis (largest biologics customer, Librela supply).

customers.bms: Bristol-Myers Squibb: 25+ year partnership (BBRC, India's first dedicated R&D centre), 700+ scientists; extended to 2035 with wider scope across discovery, translational, development, manufacturing and clinical (q3call Jan-2026; q4call; AR26 MD&A). Growth expected around US inflation (Peter Bains, q4call).
customers.zoetis: Long-term partnership signed 2018 for commercial-scale biologics manufacturing (q1ppt p.8): a 10-year programme with potential of up to US$500 mn; early years ran above the average as channels were filled (CFO, q3call). Librela (bedinvetmab, Zoetis's anti-NGF antibody for canine osteoarthritis pain) went into destocking from the start of FY26 and a 'product issue' (CFO, q3call). Q1/Q2FY27 'almost no Librela', minor volumes late in FY27 (q4call); 'not completely zero'; Zoetis holds inventory for the next couple of years; impact 'nearly $50 million' (q1call). Syngene has no role in the follow-on molecule Lenivia beyond some clinical work (q4call).
customers.src: ar26 note 33; q3call; q4call; q1call; q1ppt

commentary: FY27 'a year of transition', 'course correction, strategic renewal'; single-digit rupee revenue decline (mid-single-digit, CFO) and EBITDA margins in the mid-20s; return to growth from FY28 (Q4 guide had been broadly flat revenue)
Revenue -16%: absence of Zoetis offtake plus attrition of a few clients in commoditised research services that Syngene chose not to chase on price
Operating EBITDA margin 12% after a Rs50 cr forex hedge loss; partly offset by cost cuts in people and other expenses
Mangaluru (small-molecule API) had very low utilisation in past years; lock-ins for commercial and clinical molecules, significant ramp-up in FY27 and FY28
Unit 3 (Stelis) customers signed and batches taken, but mostly clinical/development molecules; no large-volume commercial molecule yet
Bayview (US) to be operationalised later in FY27; one or two US projects converted; revenue from FY28; not capitalised in FY27, so minimal P&L cost
BIOSECURE and the listing of Chinese companies give an advantage to shift molecules from China to India; tariffs and 'Make in US' help the US site
Net cash Rs1,541 cr at Jun-26 vs Rs1,800 cr at Mar-26: seasonal, customer advances arrive in Jan-Mar and are used through the year

otherIncomeNote.note: Company other income excludes forex (the hedge loss sits inside operating EBITDA). Screener's other income nets exceptional items (FY26 -Rs9 cr; Q1FY27 Rs12 cr)
otherIncomeNote.src: ar26 consolidated note 19; q1ppt p.26; q4ppt p.26

treasury.note: Screener puts cash Rs833 cr and investments Rs741 cr (incl. Rs39.7 cr of strategic unlisted stakes such as Immuneel) at Mar-26 but leaves the Rs275.4 cr of bank deposits over 12 months in other financial assets; the model adds them back (otherTreasury). Company net cash excludes Rs449 cr of lease liabilities.

capacity.biologics: Total single-use bioreactor capacity to 50,000 L once Bayview is integrated (AR26 note 43; q1ppt p.8)
capacity.unit3: Acquired from Stelis Biopharma (Strides group) by slump sale effective 1-Dec-2023: announced Jul-2023 at Rs702 cr (~$86 mn) for 20,000 L of drug-substance capacity, closed at a revised gross value of Rs617 cr (some equipment retained by Stelis); licensed and capitalised in Q1FY26; 8 kL line commissioned out of 20 kL; GMP bioconjugation (ADC) suite and bioassay lab added in FY26; took ~18 months to get operational (CFO, q4call)
capacity.bayview: Bought from Emergent BioSolutions (Emergent Manufacturing Operations Baltimore) in Mar-2025 for US$36.5 mn; asset acquisition: Rs298 cr in CWIP + Rs31 cr land at Mar-25, plus Rs78.5 cr of pre-operating costs capitalised into CWIP in FY26; 2 kL and 4 kL single-use bioreactors; qualification complete (Jan-2026); operationalisation later in FY27, capitalisation after regulatory approvals (not in FY27)
capacity.mangaluru: Commercial small-molecule API plant; 'very low utilisation in the past years' (CEO, q1call); a sterile fill-finish line installed at the Mangaluru large-molecule site (q3call)
capacity.src: ar26 notes 3, 43, MD&A pp.188-189; stelisAnn; stelis; reuters (10-Mar-2025); q3call; q4call; q1call
